description: The bar chart illustrates the token count for two distinct prompting strategies—“Reasoning” (orange) and “Demonstration” (blue)—across varying numbers of shots (0 through 4), as part of a graph-based analysis of reasoning in large language models. The vertical axis, labeled “Token Count,” ranges from 0 to 7000 in increments of 1000, while the horizontal axis, labeled “Number of Shots,” displays discrete integer values from 0 to 4. At 0 shots, only the “Reasoning” bar is present, with a token count of 6393. For 1 through 4 shots, each category is represented by a stacked bar: the lower orange segment corresponds to “Reasoning” and the upper blue segment to “Demonstration.” Red downward-pointing arrows with negative values (–1952, –1613, –1040, –1379) are overlaid on the bars for shots 1–4, indicating the token reduction attributable to the “Demonstration” component relative to the baseline “Reasoning” token count at 0 shots. The “Reasoning” portion of the stacked bars decreases slightly as the number of shots increases, while the “Demonstration” portion varies across shot counts, contributing to the overall token count for each condition. The chart visually emphasizes how adding demonstration examples affects total token usage compared to pure reasoning prompts.
